localChanges: A defender beaten in a city of size 1 now counts as a loss in the Military report wherever its home city was (closes #1000).
A unit lost with a transport its city disbanded, or Settlers lost to famine, no longer cost their city another unit for want of shields.
Pillage takes Irrigation or a Mine first, then the Railroad, then the Road, and never Pollution, as in Civilization (closes #1061).
With the Pyramids, a Democracy brought down by civil disorder now falls into Anarchy, and you can choose a new government straight away (closes #1018).
A fight with the Barbarians no longer ends world peace in the score (closes #956).

log: `buildWithProduction` works from the yields worked out at the start, so it could hand the `Unsupported` rules a unit destroyed since: the cargo of a transport just disbanded at sea (even by this same loop), or Settlers lost to famine. That unit was destroyed, and announced, a second time, and a living unit could be disbanded for support the dead one no longer used. Now, while the city is short, a destroyed unit's support is given back before any more living units go, and it isn't lost again. With production to spare, its support for the turn is still owed, as before (civ-clone/web-renderer#1000). This applies to every game that uses this package, Civilization II's included.

With civ1-unit's `unit/defeated/emit-and-destroy` now High, a defender beaten in a city of size 1 is destroyed by the attacker's win, and counted as a loss, before the city shrinks, as v474.05's `battle` drops it before `vanish` removes the city. Before, a defender the city supported, or every unit of a player losing its last city, was destroyed by no one as the city went, so the loss wasn't counted, and then again by the win (civ-clone/web-renderer#1000). This needs civ1-unit with that change.

`lib/defendersLosing` is no longer needed and is gone. `unit/defeated/emit` is gone too: civ1-unit's rule already announces the defeat, so `unit:defeated` was raised twice. `unit/defeated/shrink-defended-city` stays at the usual priority, so later `Defeated` rules (the computer player's) still find a city of size 1 gone, and it now does nothing if the city has gone already.

A government that civil disorder brings down now falls into Anarchy at once, however short a rule makes the Anarchy. With the Pyramids the Anarchy lasts no turns, so the player stayed a Democracy and the collapse changed nothing. v474.05 calls `set_government(selected_owner, 0)` whatever Wonders the player has, and the Pyramids end the Anarchy at the `city_phase` that follows the cities being worked that turn. So the new government can be chosen straight away, and the cities still to be judged for disorder and celebration that turn see Anarchy (civ-clone/web-renderer#1018). A chosen revolution with the Pyramids still skips Anarchy.
civ1-city-happiness's collapse test and the renderer's "Thanks to the Pyramids" notice both assume the old behaviour, and need companion changes when this is taken up.

`unit/defeated/world-peace` now leaves the count alone when either side of the fight is the Barbarians, as v474.05's `battle` does (`if (attacker_civ && defender_civ) player_peace_run = 0;`, where the Barbarians are civ 0). So a player who only fights off Barbarians keeps the world peace bonus in the score (civ-clone/web-renderer#956). This matches civ2-score, which also resets only on a fight between two civilizations.

`unit/defeated/emit-and-destroy` is now High, so a beaten unit is destroyed, and counted as a loss to the winner, before any other package's `Defeated` rule runs, before civ1-city shrinks or destroys the city it defended. This is v474.05's order: `battle` drops the defender before `vanish` removes a city of size 1. Shrinking first destroyed a defender the city supported, or every unit of a player losing its last city, by no one, so the loss went uncounted (civ-clone/web-renderer#1000).

`unit/destroyed/emit` and `unit/destroyed/count-loss` now check, as their effects run, whether the unit is already destroyed. A unit destroyed again, after its destruction or from inside it (when its loss defeats its player, and the defeat destroys its units), now raises `unit:destroyed` and counts as a loss only once.

Registers a Civ1 `PillageTarget` rule (base-unit-action-pillage's `pillageTarget`, `civ1-unit:unit/pillage-target`) with v474.05's order from `CONTROL.C`'s 'P' command: Irrigation or a Mine, else the Railroad, else the Road. Until now `Pillage` took the first improvement on the square, so a polluted square with a Road could lose its Pollution and keep the Road (civ-clone/web-renderer#1061). The list pillage is offered for and the list it takes from are now one export, `pillageable`, from `pillageOrder`.
